standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness is preserved by base change of the quotients by the powers of an ideal, so the flatness of the map gives flatness of the induced maps of quotients
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the equivalence of the first two conditions to a criterion about quotients.

standard_prerequisites.name: A flat map of rings is faithfully flat exactly when the induced map on spectra is surjective, which for the quotients is the same as being an isomorphism of the quotients
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the equivalence of the first two conditions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Modules annihilated by the ideal are modules over the quotient, and the base change along the map agrees with the base change along the induced map of quotients
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the third condition with the first, and later allows the faithfulness statement to be applied to the quotients.

core_obligations: Observe that flatness of the map makes the induced maps of the quotients flat, and invoke the faithful flatness criterion for quotients to conclude that the first two conditions are equivalent (proof lines 24241-24245).

Identify modules annihilated by the ideal with modules over the quotient and the base change along the map with the base change along the induced map of quotients, obtaining the equivalence of the first and third conditions (proof lines 24245-24251).

Record that the fourth condition implies the third immediately, and assume the third in order to prove the fourth: use flatness of the quotients and the surjectivity on spectra to see that the base change functor is faithful on modules annihilated by any fixed power of the ideal (proof lines 24251-24257).

Conclude for arbitrary power torsion modules by writing such a module as the union of the submodules annihilated by the successive powers and using that the tensor product commutes with colimits, which gives the last equivalence (proof lines 24257-24260).
proof_roadmap: Flatness of the quotients plus the faithful flatness criterion gives the first equivalence (proof lines 24241-24245).
Identify modules annihilated by the ideal with modules over the quotient to get the third condition (proof lines 24245-24251).
Pass from the fixed powers to arbitrary power torsion modules by colimits (proof lines 24251-24260).
difficulty_reason: The statement gives four equivalent conditions on a ring map and an ideal: flatness with faithful flatness of the quotients, flatness with surjectivity on spectra of the quotients, flatness with faithfulness of base change on modules annihilated by the ideal, and flatness with faithfulness on all power torsion modules (statement lines 24226-24239). The proof moves along the cycle by standard reductions: flatness descends to the quotients, faithful flatness is surjectivity on spectra, modules annihilated by the ideal are modules over the quotient against which the base change functor is compared, and an arbitrary power torsion module is the union of the modules annihilated by the successive powers, which reduces the last condition to the previous one through commutativity of the tensor product with colimits (proof lines 24241-24260). The identification of the base change functor with the one over the quotient is the step that makes the third condition computable.
